summary: A fatal engine startup crash reaches the user as a generic readiness timeout. Two unrelated sub-second crashes (missing sqlalchemy; SIGILL) produced the identical "failed to become ready in time" message while the real traceback sat in app.log. ensureServerRunning does not distinguish an already-exited child from one still starting. Exposed by ComfyUI core failing on a pre-AVX2 CPU: kornia_rs 0.1.14 SIGILLs at import through init_builtin_extra_nodes -> nodes_post_processing -> kornia, so no node-level opt-out exists. Global kornia_rs pin REJECTED. ISA floor UNCONFIRMED - do not publish a hardware requirement without disassembling the wheel.
Implementation started and completed same session, at the user request to address the GPU-affecting half.

FIXED and live-verified. Two holes, one root cause - the startup path could not tell "still starting" from "already dead": the poll loop tested only check.ready and ignored running:false, and /comfy/start's 500 body was discarded. Now processState.lastComfyExit records code/signal/deliberate plus a 15-line output tail, /comfy/status returns it, the poll aborts the moment the process is gone, and _describeComfyExit renders one actionable sentence. Live on the Linux box: real crash caught in 3s with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named sqlalchemy captured verbatim, vs the full 60s timeout before. Real payloads rendered through the shipped function; assertions cover missing-module, SIGILL, and the no-output fallback. eslint clean. CPU-specific halves (kornia pin, CPU preflight, docs hardware floor) DROPPED per the user call that CPU inference is a fallback nobody uses - the timeout masking is NOT CPU-specific and is what was fixed. Remote/Pod start path untouched.
Archived out of board.columns.done to .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/_archived/MPI-415/ (workspace preserved intact). mpi-archive run 2026-08-04.
